raw_response:
*reasoning in my voice*

Aiyo, what is there to say? I've been farming this little patch for 30 years — my old man and me, just the two of us at home now, the children work in the city. 4.1 mu isn't much, but it feeds us and brings in a few yuan when the harvest is good.

I don't think too hard about this every year. I do what I've always done, same as my mother before me, same as my neighbors. When the weather starts turning cool, early October, after we're done resting from the maize harvest, we plant the wheat. All 4.1 mu goes to wheat — there's nothing else to grow in winter here. I buy seed from the little shop in town, same kind as last year, about 15 kg per mu. I don't save seed — the shop seed comes up better, my neighbor Xiuying told me so years ago.

For fertilizer, before planting I put down one bag of the red compound — one 50-kg bag for each mu — the 15-15-15 kind, everyone uses it. When the wheat wakes up in spring and starts growing tall, I scatter urea, about half a bag per mu. If the wheat looks pale I'll put a little more. I don't measure with a scale, I know by the feel of the scoop.

Water — I turn on the well maybe four times: once before it freezes, once when it greens up, once when it's standing up tall, once more when the grain is filling. Electricity for pumping isn't cheap, so I don't water more than I need to. My old man does the sprayer work — a little herbicide in the spring for the weeds, that's all. Bugs don't bother wheat much here.

June, we cut the wheat. I hire the combine man, 50 yuan per mu. Too tired now to do it by hand like when I was young. Right away — within three or four days — we have to get the maize in. No time to plow. The tractor man comes with the direct-seeder and puts the maize straight into the stubble. Mid-June. Hybrid maize seed, always — everyone buys it now, it yields much better than what my mother used to plant.

For maize I put one bag of compound at seeding and then topdress urea when the leaves get big, maybe a bit less than for wheat. If it rains enough in July and August I don't water. If it's dry when the tassels come out, I'll water once — that's the important time, Wang's auntie next door always reminds everyone. End of September, start of October, the picker comes and we're done.

Yields? In a normal year I get around 400 kg of wheat and around 500 kg of maize per mu. Some years less. Last year the maize was thin because it rained too much in August and the cobs didn't fill well. The year before was good. You can't know ahead of time. So I don't change what I do — changing is risky and I don't have savings to take chances with.
